body_ar:
الله سبحانه وتعالى موصوف بكل كمال منزه عن كل نقص، ولهذا فإن من عقيدة أهل السنة والجماعة أنهم يثبتون لله عز وجل ما أثبته لنفسه أو أثبته له رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم، وينفون عنه سبحانه ما نفاه عن نفسه أو نفاه عنه رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم، ومن ذلك إثبات صفة الحكم والاستفهام لخلقه وهو أعلم بهم، وأنه لا ند له ولا نظير ولا يعجزه شيء سبحانه وتعالى.
إثبات صفة الحكم لله عز وجل:
يقول الشيخ حفظه الله: يحكم بالحق يستفهم وهو أعلم. كذلك من الصفات المثبتة لله سبحانه وتعالى صفة الحكم، فقد أثبتها لنفسه في كثير من الآيات، وإثباتها في القرآن جاء بصيغة الفعل، وجاء بصيغة الاسم بالحصر: فصيغة الاسم مثل قول الله تعالى على لسان يعقوب ويوسف عليهما السلام: إِنِ الْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ [يوسف:67] ، فيعقوب عليه السلام يقول: إِنِ الْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ وَعَلَيْهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُتَوَكِّلُونَ [يوسف:67] ، ويوسف عليه السلام يقول: إِنِ الْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ أَمَرَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ [يوسف:40] ، وكذلك قول الله تعالى: وَمَا اخْتَلَفْتُمْ فِيهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَحُكْمُهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ [الشورى:10]....
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* God, glorified and exalted is He, is described by every perfection and is free of every deficiency. For this reason it belongs to the creed of the People of the Sunnah and the Community that they affirm for God, mighty and majestic, what He has affirmed for Himself or what His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, has affirmed for Him, and that they deny of Him, glorified is He, what He has denied of Himself or what His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, has denied of Him. Of this is the affirmation of the attribute of judging, and of His putting questions to His creation while He knows them best, and that He has no equal and no peer, and that nothing can thwart Him, glorified and exalted is He.

## Affirming the attribute of judgement for God, mighty and majestic

The Sheikh, may God preserve him, says: *He judges by the truth; He asks, and He knows best.*

Likewise, among the attributes affirmed for God, glorified and exalted is He, is the attribute of judgement (ḥukm). He has affirmed it for Himself in many verses, and its affirmation in the Qur'an comes in the form of a verb, and comes in the form of a noun with exclusivity.

The noun form is as in the words of God, exalted is He, on the tongue of Jacob and Joseph, peace be upon them both: {Judgement belongs to none but God} (Sūrat Yūsuf 12:67). Jacob, peace be upon him, says: {Judgement belongs to none but God; in Him I have placed my trust, and in Him let all who trust place their trust} (Sūrat Yūsuf 12:67). And Joseph, peace be upon him, says: {Judgement belongs to none but God. He has commanded that you worship none but Him} (Sūrat Yūsuf 12:40). And likewise the words of God, exalted is He: {And in whatever you differ, its judgement rests with God} (Sūrat al-Shūrā 42:10)….

flags.context: صفة الحكم ... إِنِ الْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ
flags.note: The passage is about ḥukm as a divine attribute, and 'judgement' is the reading the context requires. The rendering matters because 'إن الحكم إلا لله' has a separate twentieth-century political career in which it is read as 'sovereignty belongs to God alone'; nothing in this record supports that reading and the English must not import it. Recorded so that no later editor substitutes the political sense.

flags.context: the line of the versified base text quoted at the head of the section
options: He asks, and He knows best
He puts questions, though He knows best
He enquires while being the most knowing
flags.note: The attribute of istifhām: God putting a question to a creature whose answer He already knows. 'Though' would insert a concessive the Arabic does not have and would make the act sound like a difficulty to be explained away; the flatter 'and' is used. The record stops before the Sheikh treats this attribute at all.

translator_notes: One of a run of fourteen records, IDs 734-747, the series 'The Names and Attributes', all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and the first lines of a lesson, and then breaks off on an ellipsis; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/esmawesivat-* series, numbered 1 to 14 in the same order as the IDs.

The source's final line, 'تحميل المادة' ('download the material'), is the label of a download link in the page furniture, not part of the text. It is recorded as source_download_link and omitted from body_ar and body_en.

This record does carry a CMS timestamp in a .create_date span (10 May 2011, within a 28-minute window shared by the whole run 738-747). That is a bulk-upload timestamp for the series, not the date the lesson was given, and it is not evidence of composition date. Record 737, translated in an earlier wave, reports no date for this run; the timestamp is in fact present in the page and should be backfilled there.
Qur'anic renderings here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.
Creedal material. Per style guide section 8, the vocabulary of divine attributes is not the vocabulary of the five legal rulings and the five-rulings mapping is not applied anywhere in this record.

The synopsis announces four topics — judgement, God's questioning of His creation, His having no equal or peer, and nothing being able to thwart Him. Only the first is reached before the record stops, and even that stops after the scriptural citations and before any explanation. Marked critical_for_display.
The source's own bracketed verse references are kept in body_ar exactly as served and converted to the house form in body_en.
